timing: after confirmatory asset acquisition and pose-support diagnostic, before any U3b reconstruction or Chamfer outcome
problem: The original preflight implementation requires finite scene medians for both pose interpretations and throws when the inverse interpretation produces zero valid cross-projection support. The frozen U3b prose did not specify this undefined-control case.

clarifiedPassRule.normalCase: If the inverse interpretation has at least one supported frozen pair, retain the original U3b rule unchanged: camera-to-world must win a majority of mutually comparable pairs and have a lower scene median cross-projection depth disagreement than the inverse interpretation.
clarifiedPassRule.zeroInverseSupportCase: If the inverse interpretation has zero supported frozen pairs, classify it as geometrically dominated only if camera-to-world has finite support on every one of the 16 frozen pairs. In that case the scene passes the pose-convention gate without inventing an inverse median.

rationale: Zero inverse support is not evidence that camera-to-world lacks geometric support when camera-to-world remains valid on all fixed pairs. Requiring 16/16 camera-to-world support distinguishes wrong-pose projection-out from a scene-level overlap failure while adding no new pairs, no smaller stride, no replacement scene and no reconstruction metric exposure.
nonChanges: No new confirmatory scene is selected.
No validation pair is added or replaced.
No TSDF reconstruction or FARO Chamfer result has been generated.
The U3b geometry gate and shuffled-confidence gate remain unchanged.
claimPolicy: This clarification must be disclosed as a pre-reconstruction adapter/preflight clarification prompted by an undefined inverse-control case observed after asset acquisition. It does not convert U3b into a fully untouched-from-acquisition protocol, but it preserves confirmatory geometry evaluation because no treatment geometry outcome informed the clarification.
